**Three issues to raise with your lead before shipping.** None of these require restructuring.

1. **The description will hurt triggering.** Claude decides whether to load a skill based mostly on the `description`. "Anything related to our company" gives it no concrete keywords, so it may not load when someone asks about a rollback or a specific alert. You can keep one skill and just make the description more specific:
   > `description: Company handbook covering Python/TypeScript code style, deploy and rollback steps for our 4 services, on-call runbook for all alert types, PTO and expense policy, brand voice for marketing copy, org chart and contacts, and glossary of internal terms. Use when writing code, deploying, handling alerts or incidents, answering HR/policy questions, writing marketing copy, finding who owns something, or decoding internal jargon.`

2. **All 3,000 lines load every time the skill triggers.** A glossary question would also pull in the full runbook and style guide. That costs context and can dilute answers. If you want to fix this later, you can still keep one skill: move each section into its own file in the same folder (e.g., `runbook.md`, `deploy.md`) and have SKILL.md link to them. Claude then reads only the file it needs, and you still maintain one skill. This is optional, and pasting everything in works today.

3. **Phone numbers in the org chart.** Personal contact info ends up in model context and anywhere the skill folder is shared or synced. Consider whether you need numbers in there or whether names, roles, and a pointer to the directory are enough. You may need to check with whoever owns privacy/HR.

If the lead wants it exactly as specified, the block above is ready to paste into.
